To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
genetic variants of DNA ligase IV, an enzyme involved in non-homologus end joining (Nhej), can affect the risk for developing multiple myelomas.

genetic variants of DNA ligase IV, which is involved in the non-homologus end joining pathway of DNA double strand break repair, can affect the risk developing multiple myelomma, a tumour characterized by aberrant class switching recombination.

the A3V and the T9L polymorphisms of the LIG 4 gene, which is involved in DSB repair by non homologous end joining, are associated with a reduced risk of multiple myeloma and that the A3T and T9L variant alleles are in complete linkage disequilibrium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
investigating the impact that genetic variants of DNA repair genes have upon predisposition and prognosis in cancer.

the role of genetic variants in the DNA double stranded break repair gene, NHEJ DNA Ligase IV, in the development of lymphoproliverative disease, including leukaemias, lymphomas and multiple myelomas.
the role of genetic variants of the NHEJ Ligation 4 DNA ligase in the aetiological mechanisms of multiple myeloma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LIG4 polymorphism A3V is associated with a reduced risk of multiple myeloma.
genetic variants of DNA repair genes, including NHEJ DNA Ligase IV, can modulate susceptibility to multiple myelomas.
the LIG4 variants identified in our studies do not have an effect on risk of developing lymphoproliferation in general.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the A3V and the T9L variants of NHE4LIG4 may reduce susceptibility to multiple myelomas, and that this effect is the result of inheritance the A3V-9L haplotypes.

the LIG4 variants we have identified are likely to be involved in the aetiogenesis of multiple myeloma and that the A3V and/or T9I variants are likely to act as protective alleles against the development of this disease.

genetic variants within LIG4 may influence the predisposition to multiple-myeloma by altering the efficiency of the DNA DSB repair mechanism, nonhomologous end-joining, a process believed to be intimately related to class-switch recombination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LIG4 is a potential candidate gene for predisposition to multiple Myeloma.
LIG4 polymorphic variants can affect the risk for developing multiple myelomas.
the A3V and I9T polymorphisms are in LD, and that the haplotype formed by these two SNPs (A3V-T9T) may be a risk factor for multiple myeloma.
